title: In Savage Africa
subtitle: or, Six Years of Adventure in Congo-Land
summary: Edward James Glave (1863–1895), a young Englishman, went to the Congo in 1883 in the service of the International Association, under H. M. Stanley, who writes the introduction. He gives an account of his six years there: the voyage out and the march past the lower river, his command of the station at Lukolela, his neighbours and their customs, charm doctors, hunting of buffalo, elephant, and hippopotamus, and a stay at Bolobo. After a visit home he returned in 1886 for the Sanford Exploring Expedition, trading in ivory on the river and its tributaries, and he describes slave raiding, the people of the Oubangi, and Tippu Tib. He left the Congo in 1889. The book has many drawings, some from his own sketches, and a map. It uses the language of its time about Africans.
